Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331, missingbulb/Claudinite#1336

{"total_count":80,"workflow_runs":[{"id":32728401283,"name":"Claudinite executor","display_title":"Claudinite executor","workflow_id":336228267,"run_number":151,"run_attempt":1,"event":"workflow_dispatch","status":"completed","conclusion":"success","head_branch":"main","head_sha":"05bc710a34cef772bf9b8d5053e76350fd50d87d","head_commit":{"message":"Repoint the queue workflows at the claudinite-tasks mount, and name the secrets again (#258)

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331, missingbulb/Claudinite#1336

input.title: The claudinite-tasks seed migration is not declaring the pack on converged members
input.body:
Read from each member's own tree after L1's sweep (#1330) and L2's PRs merged:

| Mounts `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/` | Declares `claudinite-tasks` in `.claudinite-settings.json` |
|---|---|
| ClaudiniteCanary, ClaudiniteWebsite, CrosswordChat, EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, Shepherd, hitbut, VascularColoring, WIP | ClaudiniteCanary, Shepherd only |

`packs/claudinite-tasks/migrations/2026-08-24-claudinite-tasks-seed/` exists to declare the pack into every member that carries a scheduler workflow, and all nine carry one. Seven converged past it without gaining the entry.

Nothing is broken today, which is why this is easy to miss: the pack is on disk in all nine because #1335's engine-lane tolerance vendors it regardless of declaration, and both workflows now reach its queue modules by literal path. But an undeclared pack contributes no prose, no checks, no skills and no tasks — so those seven are running the queue while the pack that owns it is inert for every session and every check.

**Why it blocks L4.** The tolerance and the legacy shims are what L4 removes. The moment either goes, "mounted but undeclared" stops being harmless, so the declaration has to be true on every member before that PR (#1329) can land.

What to establish, in order:

- [ ] Whether the migration ran at all on those members, or ran and declared nothing — its `appliesTo` probes for `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, which all nine have.
- [ ] Whether ClaudiniteCanary and Shepherd got their entry from the migration or from some other path (adoption, a hand edit), since a false positive here would send the fix in the wrong direction.
- [ ] The fix, and a forced converge that shows the entry arriving on a member that lacks it — not a passing test alone.

Refs #1317, #1331

input.description: Read the design on stored prompts

content.content:
secret-shaped half in the repo's config where `required_secrets` already
lives.

**The endpoint is a ROUTINE's API trigger, and that moves where the agent's
instructions live** (verified against the routines documentation at
implementation, not assumed): firing a routine runs *its* saved prompt, and the
`text` we send arrives wrapped in a block explicitly labelled untrusted, which a
routine acts on only because its stored prompt says to. So the payload names the
item and the nonce and instructs nothing, and the prompt is a tracked artifact —
— [`packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md`](../../packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md),
which the routine's stored prompt does nothing but point at, one line long. The issue-is-data posture arrives intact at one more
hop: behavior comes from files under review, never from what an API caller sent.
A routine's repository scope is then the whole meaning of an endpoint, which is
what makes "reach is which endpoint you name" true in the deployment and not only
in the design.

**The token must be usable from the GitHub Action, and the plumbing is the
`required_secrets` plumbing, reused exactly**: the executor job — the *only* place
invocation happens — reads the endpoint's named secret out of the same bag every
task's secrets come from.
This works because Actions secrets are reachable Action-side and nowhere else
===
hours are written once at adoption, and `run:` lines name **mount pack paths**
(`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`) behind which everything converges nightly — a
release never edits the YAML again.

Consequently **no update flow touches `.github/workflows/`**, and the `pending-workflows/`
withhold lane does not exist: a structural change to the YAML itself (permissions, an actions
version bump) is an explicit, human-merged fleet PR event, not a lane the machinery must carry.
Adoption of `claudinite-tasks` (the adopt-pack skill, or bootstrap when the pack is declared at
init) scaffolds the two files and the CCR routine endpoints; the routines' stored prompts point
at the pack's operational documents in the mount.

Members' `claudinite-ci.yml` is untouched by any of this: it is seeded once by bootstrap when no
existing workflow runs the world sweep, is member-owned from then on, and belongs to the checks
surface.

### Alternatives considered

- **Scheduler in the engine.** Scheduling was 52% of core; every consumer vendored machinery
  only scheduled repos use, engine releases implied workflow-path churn, and "core" stopped
  meaning distribution. Rejected — the size and the boundary rot are what this boundary fixes.
- **Fold the queue into claudinite-lifecycle.** Removes the updates↔queue seam entirely, but

skip this — dropping the row is a real choice, so don't re-seed one the repo removed on purpose.

**Adopting `claudinite-tasks` also scaffolds the two workflow files** — the scheduler run with
its drain, and the label-event executor:

```
node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs <owner/repo>
```

`.github/workflows/` is the one directory a member's nightly may never push to, so these arrive
here or not at all. They are static from this moment: the cron minute is hashed from the repo's
full name, both anchor hours come from its `taskScheduler.dailyHour`, and every `run:` names a
mount path behind which the code converges nightly. The command is a no-op when both files are
already right. A repo adopting this pack also needs its two CCR routine endpoints — the executor's
and the work-item session's — pointed at `executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md` in its own
mount; that is a console setting, so it belongs in the handover issue §4b files.

## 4. Scaffold what the pack now demands

A newly active pack may require structure the repo doesn't have yet — deliberately, so the
declaration is a statement of intent that its own findings then guide you to satisfy. Run the
world sweep and let each finding name the file: e.g. `product-wiki` wants its index and the
reviewed `product-requirements/` sink before the isolation wall has anything to guard. Scaffold
per the pack's own README template; the pack's rules are the checklist.

## 4b. File what adoption cannot do

A pack may declare `adoptionHandover` — steps only a human can perform (a repository or
console setting, a permission, a secret). The install runner prints them; they are not
optional and they are not PR-body notes. **Open one tracking issue per adopting repo**,
a checkbox per step, carrying each step's `breaks` (what is broken while it is off) and
`done` (its closing condition) verbatim. Per-repo manual work reliably does not happen,
so an unfiled step is a capability that dies silently in that member.

Say on the adoption PR that the issue exists and link it. If the repo already has an
open issue for the same steps, comment there rather than opening a second.

## 5. Land

World and work checks green (`.claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`; the Stop hook

If this file is current, that # whole lane worked. # # Hence `workflow_dispatch` and nothing else: no schedule, no push, no pull_request. # What is under test is whether the file ARRIVES. The update commits with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, GitHub refuses that token under that path, and the refusal rejects the **whole ref** — so a single workflow write does not fail one file, it fails the entire converge and everything riding it. #649 is that problem. The answer is the **withhold lane** in [`updates/pack-update.mjs`](../../updates/pack-update.mjs): every write bound for `.github/workflows/` is diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, a path the Action token *can* push. It rides the maintenance PR as an ordinary added file — reviewable in the diff, recoverable if nothing else runs — and the update ends at `apply-stage` until a session holding an MCP credential moves it into place. That lane shipped with **one** exercised caller: the scheduler workflow's own convergence. A record's `materialize` goes through the same `write`, and had never run against a live member — the residual #649 was reopened for, and the last item left on #768. Proving it needs a record that materializes a workflow into a repo that really runs the update flow, and nothing in the corpus was one. ## What happened

`instructions.md` step 6 tells the session to converge its work item by running:

```
node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue  --outcome ... --summary ... [--pr ]
```

`converge-item.mjs`'s `main()` wires this to `makeGh()` from `signals/gh.mjs`, which does a raw `fetch` to `api.github.com` authenticated with `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN`. In this session type (a Claude Code cloud/web session with the GitHub MCP connector, invoked here via the scheduler's routine-fire endpoint), that call is rejected outright:

```
HTTP 403
{"message":"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization.","documentation_url":"https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/github-actions"}
```

This session's only working GitHub channel is the GitHub MCP connector (`mcp__github__*` tools) — consistent with this session's own system instructions ("You do NOT have access to the gh CLI, hub CLI, or direct GitHub API access. Instead, use the GitHub MCP server tools ... for ALL GitHub interactions."). Running `converge-item.mjs` with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` set fails immediately with `converge-item: #236 could not be read`, because the injected `gh()` never gets a successful response.

## Why this isn't a one-off

The codebase already recognizes this exact split for PR delivery: `land-pr.mjs` is explicitly "Action-side" raw-fetch, and `deliver-pr.md` beside it is the documented **agent-lane MCP twin**, with a comment noting "your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools." No equivalent prose or code twin exists for `converge-item.mjs`, even though `instructions.md` (also vendored) directs the session — not an Action — to invoke it directly.

## Impact on this run

Item #236's actual work succeeded (the two withheld workflow files were delivered byte-for-byte, `selftest --strict` and `check_the_world.mjs` passed clean, and PR #237 was merged into `main`). But the session could not perform the terminal convergence in code as instructed, and per the queue instructions ("nothing below is yours to perform... doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`"), it did not hand-rewrite the item's labels/close state either. #236 is being left as-is for the standing executing-leash reclaim to pick up.

## Suggested remedy

Either give `converge-item.mjs` an injectable GitHub client so an agent session can supply one backed by MCP, or add an MCP-lane prose/code twin analogous to `deliver-pr.md`, so `instructions.md` step 6 is actually performable by the session type it's written for.

## What happened

`instructions.md` step 6 tells the session to converge its work item by running:

```
node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue  --outcome ... --summary ... [--pr ]
```

`converge-item.mjs`'s `main()` wires this to `makeGh()` from `signals/gh.mjs`, which does a raw `fetch` to `api.github.com` authenticated with `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN`. In this session type (a Claude Code cloud/web session with the GitHub MCP connector, invoked here via the scheduler's routine-fire endpoint), that call is rejected outright:

```
HTTP 403
{"message":"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization.","documentation_url":"https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/github-actions"}
```

This session's only working GitHub channel is the GitHub MCP connector (`mcp__github__*` tools) — consistent with this session's own system instructions ("You do NOT have access to the gh CLI, hub CLI, or direct GitHub API access. Instead, use the GitHub MCP server tools ... for ALL GitHub interactions."). Running `converge-item.mjs` with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` set fails immediately with `converge-item: #236 could not be read`, because the injected `gh()` never gets a successful response.

## Why this isn't a one-off

The codebase already recognizes this exact split for PR delivery: `land-pr.mjs` is explicitly "Action-side" raw-fetch, and `deliver-pr.md` beside it is the documented **agent-lane MCP twin**, with a comment noting "your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools." No equivalent prose or code twin exists for `converge-item.mjs`, even though `instructions.md` (also vendored) directs the session — not an Action — to invoke it directly.

## Impact on this run

Item #236's actual work succeeded (the two withheld workflow files were delivered byte-for-byte, `selftest --strict` and `check_the_world.mjs` passed clean, and PR #237 was merged into `main`). But the session could not perform the terminal convergence in code as instructed, and per the queue instructions ("nothing below is yours to perform... doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`"), it did not hand-rewrite the item's labels/close state either. #236 is being left as-is for the standing executing-leash reclaim to pick up.

## Suggested remedy

Either give `converge-item.mjs` an injectable GitHub client so an agent session can supply one backed by MCP, or add an MCP-lane prose/code twin analogous to `deliver-pr.md`, so `instructions.md` step 6 is actually performable by the session type it's written for.

* Repoint the queue workflows at the claudinite-tasks mount

The task surface moved out of the vendored engine into a pack, so every `run:`
line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already carries
the pack, and the canon keeps shims at the old paths until it retires them, so
both paths are live right now and this lands on its own.

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs` — the same code that scaffolds these files — rather
than hand-edited, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should carry.
The cron is unchanged: it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it. The executor's secret
names are unchanged too, regenerated from this repo's own declarations.

`.github/workflows/` is the one directory a converge cannot write, which is why
this arrives as a pull request.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331

* Drop the executor's comment about what not to put in it

Regenerated from the canon's stub after it lost the paragraph explaining why the
workflow does not serialise the whole secrets context. That is a note about an
edit rather than about the file in front of the reader, and it is pure freight
here: this file is vendored verbatim and nothing reads its comments. The reason
lives beside the code that stamps the secret list, in the pack's
converge-workflows.mjs.

* Repoint the queue workflows at the claudinite-tasks mount

The task surface moved out of the vendored engine into a pack, so every `run:`
line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already carries
the pack, and the canon keeps shims at the old paths until it retires them, so
both paths are live right now and this lands on its own.

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs` — the same code that scaffolds these files — rather
than hand-edited, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should carry.
The cron is unchanged: it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it. The executor's secret
names are unchanged too, regenerated from this repo's own declarations.

`.github/workflows/` is the one directory a converge cannot write, which is why
this arrives as a pull request.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331

* Drop the executor's comment about what not to put in it

Regenerated from the canon's stub after it lost the paragraph explaining why the
workflow does not serialise the whole secrets context. That is a note about an
edit rather than about the file in front of the reader, and it is pure freight
here: this file is vendored verbatim and nothing reads its comments. The reason
lives beside the code that stamps the secret list, in the pack's
converge-workflows.mjs.

jobs:
  scheduler-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      pickable: ${{ steps.run.outputs.pickable }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        id: run
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_WAKE: ${{ inputs.wake }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs

  drain:
    needs: scheduler-run
    # An older member workflow maps no such output, and an empty string is not
    # 'true' — so a stale copy keeps dispatching, the previous behavior and safe.
    if: needs.scheduler-run.outputs.pickable == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Start an executor for what this run readied
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/drain-dispatch.mjs

  report-failure:
    needs: [scheduler-run, drain]
    # Explicit results rather than `failure()`: `drain` is skipped on a quiet

input.title: The drain gate reads the queue before its own writes are visible, so a forced wake mints work nothing drains
input.body:
`announcePickable` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` takes the run's parting look by re-listing open issues over the REST API, immediately after the run's own writes. That read does not always see them, and when it doesn't, `pickable=false`, the drain job is skipped, and work the run just created waits for the next cron tick — up to twelve hours on the two-tick schedule.

## Seen live

ClaudiniteCanary, scheduler [run 32731101627](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/actions/runs/32731101627), dispatched with `wake: update`:

```
13:10:42.598  - created #253 claudinite-lifecycle/update (forced: it had no open standing item)
13:10:43.180  - nothing pickable — no executor is dispatched this run
```

584 ms apart. The `drain` job's `if: needs.scheduler-run.outputs.pickable == 'true'` evaluated false and the job shows `conclusion: skipped`. missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary#253 has sat `task:ready`, unclaimed, ever since — no executor run exists on that repo after 12:42.

The same repo's previous run, [32728430083](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/actions/runs/32728430083), got it right for a timing reason rather than a structural one:

```
12:41:58.162  - created #248 claudinite-lifecycle/update [task:ready]
12:41:58.738  - schedule board #148 updated (12 row(s))
12:42:05.578  - woke #236 claudinite-lifecycle/update
12:42:06.131  - 4 item(s) pickable — the drain job dispatches an executor
```

Eight seconds of other work sat between the creates and the read, and the read saw them. The failing run's only action was a single mint, so the gate read 584 ms after the write.

## Why it matters beyond one repo

This is a strong candidate for `fleet-baseline`'s recurring `did-not-converge` verdicts (#1330). The lever dispatches each member's scheduler with `wake: update`; on a member whose standing item has to be **minted** — exactly the "forced: it had no open standing item" case — the gate is at its most likely to miss, the drain skips, and the member converges nothing inside the follow window. A member that already had an open standing item has it in the list from the start and drains normally. The last two sweeps split 8/5 and 8/5.

The module's own header anticipated ordering (*"This is the run's LAST act, after the forced wake"*) but not read-after-write visibility.

## Fix direction

Don't wait, and don't re-read hoping. The run already knows what it created, readied and woke — union that set with what the list returns, and gate on the union. That removes the timing dependence entirely rather than widening a window. A sleep before the read would be the shape the corpus already rejects: a guard that names no condition.

Whatever the fix, prove it by driving a scheduler run whose *only* action is a single forced mint, and assert `pickable=true` — the passing shape above (several writes, seconds of other work) proves nothing about the failing one.

Refs #1330

```

584 ms apart. The drain job's gate read false, `drain` shows `skipped`, and [#253](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/253) has sat `task:ready` and unclaimed since — no executor has run on that repo after 12:42. The gate re-lists open issues over REST immediately after the run's own writes, and doesn't always see them. The 12:41 run got it right only because eight seconds of other work happened to sit between its creates and the read.

I filed it as **[#1340](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1340)**. It is a strong candidate for `fleet-baseline`'s recurring `did-not-converge` verdicts: the lever wakes each member with `wake: update`, and a member whose standing item must be *minted* is exactly the case most likely to miss the gate — which is why the same sweep splits 8-converged / 5-not twice running. Fix direction in the issue: gate on the union of what the run itself created and what the list returns, rather than widening a timing window.

**Two other things it surfaced:**

- Its [#239](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/239) asked to be relayed upstream — already is, as [#1149](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1149), open and labelled `quick-win`. Nothing to do but say so on the canary.
- **The canary's whole premise is gone.** `claudinite-canary-repo` and its `claudinite-workflow-probe.yml` exist, in the pack's own words, as "the canon's live proof that it can deliver a file into a member's `.github/workflows/`" via the withhold lane — which #1326 deleted. That is [#1333](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1333), and this is the concrete evidence for it: the pack, the probe workflow and the seeded revision record are all now proving a mechanism that no longer exists.

Backlog there is heavy: 29 open issues, most parked `needs-human`. Four separate `fleet-digest` items (#241, #227, #186, #157) are the predicted daily park from [#153](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/153) — `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` was never added, and the pack has no config gate for that task, so it parks every day and will keep doing so.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **[#1340](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1340)** — the drain-gate race; likely the cause of the fleet's `did-not-converge` tail. Unfixed.
> • **[ClaudiniteCanary#253](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/253)** stalled `task:ready` right now; it'll clear on the 16:00 cron, or immediately if you want me to dispatch its executor.
> • **[#1333](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1333)** — the canary's withhold-lane premise is gone; the evidence is now concrete.
> • **[ClaudiniteCanary#153](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/153)** — `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` missing, parking a `fleet-digest` item daily; four have accumulated.
> • **[#1339](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1339)** — seven members mount `claudinite-tasks` without declaring it; blocks L4.
> • **4 members** (LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR) still short of the mount, and #1340 may be why.
> • **[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** (PR D) — held for L4; needs a rebase.

Short answer: **no.** Nothing currently open would move the fleet update forward, and a couple would move it backwards.

**In the canon**, thirteen PRs are open. None of them is fleet-update work:

- **[#1327](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1327)** looks like it should be — "Extract the task execution surface into the claudinite-tasks pack" — but it's PRs A+B of the original stack, superseded by #1326 which merged as `a248483`. Its content is already in `main` by a different commit. **Close it, don't approve it.**
- **[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** (PR D, shim removal) is the tail of this migration and must *not* be approved yet — merging it now breaks every member still on the old paths. It's gated on L4, which is gated on [#1339](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1339).
- **[#1234](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1234)** says "DO NOT MERGE YET" in its own title.
- The other nine (#1303, #1299, #1285, #1284, #1283, #1204, #1157, #1152, #1031, #1021) are growth, promotion and pack-curation work. Approving them is fine on its own merits, but for the fleet it's actively counterproductive right now: each one bumps a canon version, which *widens* the gap every member has to close. Better to land them after the fleet catches up.

**In the members**, ten PRs are open across eight repos — all `rule-revalidation`, `growth-extract` and `prose-to-checks` output from their own queues. None touches the mount, the workflows or the declaration.

**What's actually blocking the fleet has no PR yet.** Two things, and I can write both:

1. **[#1340](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1340)** — the drain gate reading the queue before its own writes are visible. This is the one that matters: it's why a forced `wake: update` mints an item and nothing drains it, and it's the leading candidate for the 5 members that keep coming back `did-not-converge`. Until it's fixed, re-running `fleet-baseline` will likely keep producing the same 8/5 split.
2. **[#1339](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1339)** — the seed migration not declaring `claudinite-tasks`. Doesn't block converging, but blocks L4 and PR D.

The fastest route to a converged fleet is for me to fix #1340, land it, and then re-run the sweep — not to approve anything on the list above. Say the word and I'll start on it.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **No approvable PR advances the fleet** — the blockers ([#1340](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1340), [#1339](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1339)) are unwritten code, not pending review.
> • **[#1327](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1327)** — superseded by the merged #1326; wants closing.
> • **[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** and **[#1234](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1234)** — must stay unmerged; both are gated tails.
> • **10 canon growth/promotion PRs** — safe to approve, but each widens the version gap the fleet is chasing; better after it catches up.
> • **[ClaudiniteCanary#253](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/253)** still stalled `task:ready` from the #1340 race.

# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`
# lines below, which converge nightly — this file does not, so it must not grow
# logic. It carries no cron; the scheduler workflow's drain is the guaranteed
# delivery and a label event is latency sugar.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      continuation_depth:
        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A backstop against a wedged runner, well clear of any declared
    # `code_work_timeout`; the heartbeat's leash is what bounds real work.
    timeout-minutes: 350
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
          # Every declared task's `required_secrets`, plus the configured endpoint
          # tokens, regenerated by the wiring converge. Actions requires each secret
          # to be named statically, so this list is the whole delivery mechanism; a
          # worker then reads process.env.<NAME>.
          #
          # The converge writes the list directly beneath this line, so it stays last.
          # claudinite:secrets
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor.mjs

  continue-the-chain:
    needs: execute
    if: failure() || cancelled()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Continue the drain, or escalate a chain that keeps dying
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_CONTINUATION_DEPTH: ${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/executor-continuation.mjs

# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`
# lines below, which converge nightly — this file does not, so it must not grow
# logic. The cron is a placeholder; bootstrap and the wiring converge rewrite it
# to this repo's hashed minute and its own two anchor hours.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '10 4,16 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wake:
        description: 'Task ids to run now (`pack/task` or a bare task name, space-separated) — wakes each one’s standing item regardless of its anchor'
        required: false
        type: string

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler-run
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  scheduler-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      pickable: ${{ steps.run.outputs.pickable }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        id: run
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_WAKE: ${{ inputs.wake }}
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs

  drain:
    needs: scheduler-run
    # An older member workflow maps no such output, and an empty string is not
    # 'true' — so a stale copy keeps dispatching, the previous behavior and safe.
    if: needs.scheduler-run.outputs.pickable == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Start an executor for what this run readied
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/drain-dispatch.mjs

  report-failure:
    needs: [scheduler-run, drain]
    # Explicit results rather than `failure()`: `drain` is skipped on a quiet
    # tick, and a bare status function makes this job's fate turn on how the
    # platform propagates a skipped dependency.
    if: >-
      always()
      && (needs.scheduler-run.result == 'failure' || needs.drain.result == 'failure')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Escalate the failed run to a human-visible issue
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/workflow-failure.mjs

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/verify-in-production

# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, with a person entering
only where no automatic check can exist.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. #1121 was filed
  against a scope its PR then dropped; the verification was moot before the merge it waited on.
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## First: does this file anything at all?

Most changes **file nothing.** Run the test in this order and stop at the first answer:

1. **Did you watch it work in this session?** Then it is proven. File nothing.
2. **Did a test that ran prove it?** A unit test, a CI job, an executable-requirements or UI
   test covering exactly the behaviour that changed. File nothing — the suite is the mechanism
   that comes back.
3. **Does the change have an observable effect at all?** A comment, a design doc, a README, a
   rename with no behavioural edge, a refactor a passing suite already pins. File nothing.
4. **Otherwise: where does its effect first become observable?** If the answer is a place and a
   moment — a member repo once it converges, a site once it deploys, a session once it reloads
   its rules — that is what you file.

The bar is *could not be watched now*, not *would be nice to double-check*. A verification
filed for a change already covered by a test is a wasted run re-proving what the suite proved.

## What you file

**A deferred request** — the same ad-hoc lane `/do-later` rides, so the queue does the waiting,
the running and the lifecycle; nothing here adds machinery beside it. One issue, titled
`Verify in production: <the change, in a few words>`, its body the whole brief: the run that
verifies will never see this conversation and may be days away. Say what changed and why it
could not be watched now, then, each spelled verbatim on its own line:

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
In-production-when: <the concrete artifact to read, and what makes it true>
Verify: <what to observe, and what counts as a pass>
Not-before: <ISO instant just past the expected release>
Retry-every: <how far to push Not-before when not yet live, e.g. 1 day>
```

No `Blocked-by:`. You are filing after the merge, so the change's PR has already closed and
there is nothing left to wait on but the release itself.

- **`Original-issue:`** is where a failure lands — the issue the change was done under, which
  the run reopens if the verification fails. Make the verification that issue's **sub-issue**
  too (`mcp__github__sub_issue_write`, method `add`, `issue_number` the original,
  `sub_issue_id` the **id** the create call returned, not its number), so the change it proves
  shows what is still unproven about it — [RULES.md](../../RULES.md)' *Filing an issue that
  belongs under another*, applied where there is no PR left to carry the link.
- **`In-production-when:`** names a thing to *read*, never a duration to wait. "`missingbulb/Shepherd`'s
  `.claudinite-settings.json` stamps `packVersions.tidy-repo` at 8 or higher." "The live site's
  `/version.json` reports a version past 4.2.0." "Any session started after this landed — check
  the vendored copy under `.claudinite/shared/` carries the new text." A merge is not a
  production condition, and neither is elapsed time.
- **`Verify:`** is an assertion with a pass condition, not a topic — and a read an **unattended
  run can make**: an API response, a file at a URL, an issue's state. "Issue #100 on that repo
  is closed with a comment citing the scheduler runs" beats "check tidy-issues works". Only where no
  automatic check can exist may `Verify:` name a person's step, spelled out exactly.
- **`Not-before:`** is the queue's own wait field: adoption holds the run until the moment has
  passed. Aim it just past the release you expect — the re-arm covers a miss, so don't pad it.
- **`Retry-every:`** is the extension you are prescribing: when the run finds the change not
  yet live, it pushes `Not-before:` forward by exactly this much. Size it to the release you
  wait on — a nightly converge retries daily, a next-session rule in minutes.

Then the mark, as `/do-later` applies it: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`**, the one label the scheduler
run adopts. Beside it, in the body, **`Model: sonnet`** (reading a live artifact and judging an
assertion against it). Never `Automerge:` — a verification has nothing to merge. If the mark
doesn't exist in the repo yet, say so and leave the issue — it appears on the next scheduler run.

## Tell the run how to converge

End the body with instructions to the run itself — the issue is its whole brief, and the run
decides nothing: it executes this playbook.

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real artifact. Never infer it from a merge, a green
   run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence actually read (the version, the value,
   the URL) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen `Original-issue:` with a comment
   saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it; comment here linking
   that; close this issue as completed — the verification did its job by finding the fault.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, **clear the issue's
   `task:status:*` label** (clearing the status is the whole of the re-ask — the mark stays on
   for life), and leave the issue open. The next scheduler run re-adopts it, and the bumped
   field holds it until the new moment. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

## Then say what you filed

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, and its retry cadence.

(Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Everything checks out. Three facts that answer your questions:

**1. LaughCounter [#304](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/304) is open, `task:ready`, unclaimed since 13:10.** The update item exists — it was just never picked up.

**2. The fix reaches members without any member PR.** `engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` is a shim: `export * from '../../../packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs'`. Members still `run:` the old engine path, and it resolves into the pack. So a fix in the pack travels the ordinary converge lane into `.claudinite/shared/`.

**3. But there's a bootstrap trap, and a free way out of it.** The converge that delivers the fix is performed *by the update task* — the very thing the bug is blocking. The escape is that the item is *already minted*: a **second** scheduler dispatch will see #304 in the queue, drain, and run the update. The fleet is one re-dispatch away from converging, with or without the fix.

Doing both — fix first, so it can't recur.

Count what the scheduler run readied in its own drain gate

The gate's parting look reads the queue back from GitHub, and that read is
eventually consistent: an item created milliseconds earlier can be absent
from it. The run then reported an empty queue, skipped the drain, and left
the item it had just minted sitting `task:ready` until the next cron fire.

Observed on three members at once during the forced fleet delivery —
LaughCounter #304 created at 13:10:52.017 and reported unpickable at
13:10:52.394, 377ms later; the canary's #253 at 584ms. Each was a forced
`update`, so the delivery the force existed to make never ran.

The verdict is now the union of what the list returns with what this run
itself readied — created-as-ready, readied, reclaimed to ready, or woken.
The run does not need a read to confirm what it wrote. Ordering stays the
executor's job; this only decides whether to start one, and a run that
readied nothing over an empty queue still dispatches nothing.

Refs #1340
EOF
)" && git log -1 --format='%h %s'

input.title: Count what the scheduler run readied in its own drain gate
input.head: claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq
input.body:
The drain gate asks GitHub what is in the queue as the scheduler run's last act. That read is eventually consistent, so it can miss an item the same run created milliseconds earlier — and the run then reports an empty queue, skips the drain, and leaves the item it just minted sitting `task:ready` until the next cron fire.

This is not theoretical. It is what stalled the fleet delivery this afternoon, on three members at once:

| Member | Item | Created | Gate's verdict | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [LaughCounter#304](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/304) | `claudinite-lifecycle/update` | 13:10:52.017 | `nothing pickable` | 377 ms |
| [ClaudiniteCanary#253](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/253) | `claudinite-lifecycle/update` | 13:10:42.598 | `nothing pickable` | 584 ms |

Each was a **forced** `update` — so the delivery the force existed to make never ran, and the members stayed short of the `claudinite-tasks` mount while their schedulers ran green every hour. A run that succeeds while silently dropping its own work is the worst shape this can take: nothing is red, and the tracker reads as converged.

## What changed

The verdict is now the union of two sources rather than one read:

- what `listOpenWorkItems` returns, ordered by `pickOrder` as before;
- what **this run itself readied** — created-as-ready, readied out of blocked, reclaimed to ready, or woken by `CLAUDINITE_WAKE`.

The run does not need a read to confirm what it just wrote. `pickableCount` is exported so the seam is testable directly rather than only through the workflow's text shape.

The gate's purpose survives intact: a run that readied nothing over an empty queue still dispatches nothing, so a quiet repo still costs zero executor invocations. Ordering stays the executor's job — this only decides whether to start one, and it errs toward starting.

No sleep, no retry, no re-read.

## Delivery

`engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` re-exports this module, and members still `run:` that legacy path, so this reaches every member through the ordinary nightly converge with no member-side workflow change.

Closes #1340

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/sha/45f21f0e12e7bdca3af5b46c692875666cc0b86e/contents/.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml] # Claudinite work-item queue — the generator's scheduler run and its drain (tasks-dispatch
# DESIGN §5, §10). This is the repo's ONLY cron, and it replaces the slot
# scheduler's content at the same path when `taskScheduler.dispatch` is `"queue"`
# — same file, same hashed minute, different mechanism, so the one-cron rule and
# every reader that knows this workflow by name keep holding.
#
# A thin shim: all logic lives in the vendored engine, so this file changes
# rarely. The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap and the wiring converge
# rewrite it to this repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`.
#
# TWO JOBS, IN ORDER. The scheduler run is pure label mechanics over the issue list —
# instantiate each task's standing item at its anchor, ready what is due, reclaim
# dead executor claims — and evaluates no precondition and collects no signal. The
# drain then STARTS an executor run for what the scheduler run just created, which is what
# keeps the common case's latency at zero even with no `labeled` event delivered.
# Lost events are therefore never the only delivery — they are latency sugar,
# which is what retires the re-arm.
#
# The drain dispatches rather than executes, and that is the point: this workflow's
# concurrency group serializes SCHEDULER RUNS, and an executor run inside it would make each
# hour's scheduler run queue behind the previous hour's work — which the heartbeat, by making
# long work legal, turned from theoretical into likely (DESIGN §15.16).
#
# `workflow_dispatch` is not a convenience: it is the never-wait-for-the-cron
# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on. Its one
# input is how that lever reaches ACROSS repos: the fleet enforcer dispatches
# this workflow naming the tasks to run now, and this member wakes its own
# standing items with its own token (DESIGN §8). The alternative — the enforcer
# editing every member's issues directly — would widen the fleet PAT to issue
# writes on every repository, for a job the member can do for itself.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '39 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wake:
        description: 'Task ids to run now (`pack/task` or a bare task name, space-separated) — wakes each one’s standing item regardless of its anchor'
        required: false
        type: string

# One scheduler run at a time, always. The scheduler run's duplicate-standing-item self-heal is
# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,
# which is safe precisely because two scheduler runs never run at once.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler-run
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; a task's code_work pushes its delivery branch
  issues: write          # create / label / comment / close work items — the queue itself
  pull-requests: write   # a task's code_work opens its PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (creating a workflow_dispatch event needs write; `read` silently 403s the POST)

jobs:
  scheduler-run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_WAKE: ${{ inputs.wake }}
          # The operator hold (DESIGN §8): set this repo variable to `true` and
          # every entry point exits at its first act, having fired nothing.
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs

  # THE POST-SCHEDULER RUN DRAIN, DISPATCHED RATHER THAN RUN HERE (DESIGN §10, §15.16).
  # The scheduler run's concurrency group serializes scheduler runs — its duplicate-item self-heal
  # depends on that — and a drain running inside the group would make every hour's
  # scheduler run queue behind the previous hour's work. Since the heartbeat made long work
  # legal, that is no longer a theoretical wait. So the drain is a `workflow_dispatch`
  # of the executor workflow: it starts in its own group, on its own runner, and
  # this job's success means "the drain was started", never "the drain finished".
  #
  # This is still the guaranteed delivery. A label event may be lost; this fires
  # every hour whatever happens.
  drain:
    needs: scheduler-run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              workflow_id: 'claudinite-executor.yml',
              ref: context.payload.repository?.default_branch
                ?? context.ref.replace('refs/heads/', ''),
            });
            core.info('dispatched the executor to drain whatever this scheduler run created');

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue. Converges to ONE open
  # issue by a fixed title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a
  # first-run failure may precede any label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: [scheduler-run, drain]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            // The platform reporting its own failure IS an origin (`task:origin:github`),
            // parked in the `failure` lane — the one a person diagnoses (#1119).
            const labels = ['workflow-failure', 'task:origin:github', 'task:status:needs-human-failure'];
            const ensure = [
              { name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' },
              { name: 'task:origin:github', color: 'd4c5f9', description: 'Claudinite queue: filed by the platform itself — a workflow reporting its own failure' },
              { name: 'task:status:needs-human-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite queue: parked — the run broke, diagnose and fix' },
            ];
            for (const l of ensure) await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, ...l }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite scheduler run/drain run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels, body });

  # legal, that is no longer a theoretical wait. So the drain is a `workflow_dispatch`
  # of the executor workflow: it starts in its own group, on its own runner, and
  # this job's success means "the drain was started", never "the drain finished".
  #
  # This is still the guaranteed delivery. A label event may be lost; this fires
  # every hour whatever happens.
  drain:
    needs: scheduler-run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              workflow_id: 'claudinite-executor.yml',
              ref: context.payload.repository?.default_branch
                ?? context.ref.replace('refs/heads/', ''),
            });
            core.info('dispatched the executor to drain whatever this scheduler run created');

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue. Converges to ONE open
  # issue by a fixed title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a
  # first-run failure may precede any label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: [scheduler-run, drain]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            // The platform reporting its own failure IS an origin (`task:origin:github`),
            // parked in the `failure` lane — the one a person diagnoses (#1119).
            const labels = ['workflow-failure', 'task:origin:github', 'task:status:needs-human-failure'];
            const ensure = [
              { name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' },
              { name: 'task:origin:github', color: 'd4c5f9', description: 'Claudinite queue: filed by the platform itself — a workflow reporting its own failure' },
              { name: 'task:status:needs-human-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite queue: parked — the run broke, diagnose and fix' },
            ];
            for (const l of ensure) await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, ...l }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite scheduler run/drain run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels, body });

content.text:
Here's where it all lands.

## Your questions, answered

**Is the update task even starting?** On three of the four laggards, yes — and that made this hard to see. Their schedulers run green every hour. The update item is *minted* and then *dropped on the floor* by the same run. LaughCounter's log is unambiguous:

```
13:10:52.017  - created #304 claudinite-lifecycle/update (forced: it had no open standing item)
13:10:52.394  - nothing pickable — no executor is dispatched this run
```

377 ms. The gate asked GitHub what was in the queue, GitHub hadn't caught up with the write from a third of a second earlier, and the drain was skipped. [#304](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/304) has sat `task:ready` ever since. Same on the canary at 584 ms. **#1340 isn't a contributing factor to the stalled fleet — it is the stall.**

MissingBulbWebsite is a different and worse problem, see below.

**How does the fix reach the problematic repos?** Through the ordinary converge, with no member PR: `engine/scheduler/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` is a shim that re-exports the pack module, and members still `run:` that legacy path.

**Would it be better if I made the update PR here?** The update PR isn't a canon artifact — each member's own executor opens it in that member's repo, so I can't author it here. But you don't need one: the items are **already minted**. A second scheduler dispatch sees them and drains. I've dispatched all four (LaughCounter, ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR, ClaudiniteCanary); they're queued behind runner contention and haven't started yet, so I can't yet report them converged — I'm not going to claim a result I haven't watched.

## Landed

**[PR #1342](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1342)** — the gate's verdict is now the union of what the queue read returns with what the run itself readied (created-as-ready, readied, reclaimed-to-ready, woken). The run doesn't need a read to confirm its own writes. No sleep, no retry. `Closes #1340`. Test written first and watched fail; 741 tests green, `check_the_work` clean.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/   the drain gate unions the run's own writes with the
                                queue read; pickableCount exported so the seam is
                                testable directly, not just via workflow text shape
packs/claudinite-tasks/         version 60824.5 + VERSIONS.md row
```

## One thing I found that you should see

**MissingBulbWebsite's scheduler has failed every single run since at least Aug 22** — ~470 runs, each dying in ~2 seconds with *zero steps executed*, meaning it fails at job setup before checkout. And its `report-failure` job fails identically, so **no `workflow-failure` issue was ever filed**. It has been silently dead for days. Its logs 404 through the API, so the setup error is only visible on [the run page](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/actions/runs/32731126672). It also still carries a pre-gate workflow copy and the legacy `.claudinite-checks.json`. This is not #1340 and won't be fixed by it.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **[PR #1342](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1342)** — the #1340 fix, awaiting your review. Merging it is what stops the fleet re-stalling on the next forced delivery.
> • **Four re-dispatched schedulers queued**, not yet started — LaughCounter, ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR, ClaudiniteCanary. Their `update` items are already minted, so the second run should drain them. Unverified; say the word next turn and I'll confirm.
> • **MissingBulbWebsite is dead, not slow** — fails at job setup every run, and its own failure escalation fails too. Needs the run page opened; I can't read the setup error through the API.
> • **[#1339](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1339)** — seed migration not declaring the pack; still blocks L4 and [#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329).

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

{"id":32733952433,"name":"CI","display_title":"Count what the scheduler run readied in its own drain gate","workflow_id":317526095,"run_number":1289,"run_attempt":1,"event":"pull_request","status":"queued","head_branch":"claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq","head_sha":"9df9c682f158dc5d3560221f4b41008a447079a3","head_commit":{"message":"Count what the scheduler run readied in its own drain gate

The gate's parting look reads the queue back from GitHub, and that read is
eventually consistent: an item created milliseconds earlier can be absent
from it. The run then reported an empty queue, skipped the drain, and left
the item it had just minted sitting `task:ready` until the next cron fire.

Observed on three members at once during the forced fleet delivery —
LaughCounter #304 created at 13:10:52.017 and reported unpickable at
13:10:52.394, 377ms later; the canary's #253 at 584ms. Each was a forced
`update`, so the delivery the force existed to make never ran.

The verdict is now the union of what the list returns with what this run
itself readied — created-as-ready, readied, reclaimed to ready, or woken.
The run does not need a read to confirm what it wrote. Ordering stays the
executor's job; this only decides whether to start one, and a run that
readied nothing over an empty queue still dispatches nothing.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level of
        # nesting, so a test at an unlisted depth was silently never run — which is exactly
        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;
        # what remains is the root list, and engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the
        # moment a tracked test lands outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit;
        # adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;

The gate's parting look reads the queue back from GitHub, and that read is
eventually consistent: an item created milliseconds earlier can be absent
from it. The run then reported an empty queue, skipped the drain, and left
the item it had just minted sitting `task:ready` until the next cron fire.

Observed on three members at once during the forced fleet delivery —
LaughCounter #304 created at 13:10:52.017 and reported unpickable at
13:10:52.394, 377ms later; the canary's #253 at 584ms. Each was a forced
`update`, so the delivery the force existed to make never ran.

The verdict is now the union of what the list returns with what this run
itself readied — created-as-ready, readied, reclaimed to ready, or woken.
The run does not need a read to confirm what it wrote. Ordering stays the
executor's job; this only decides whether to start one, and a run that
readied nothing over an empty queue still dispatches nothing.
